questions.stem: What is the central idea of Data Platform Gravity?
options: Every aspect of data handling, from ingestion to transformation, analytics and deployment, is achieved within a single, unified platform
Data should be physically moved to the largest data centre
Each team should choose its own best-of-breed tool
All data must be stored on premises
Data should be replicated to every system that might need it
questions.explanation: Data Platform Gravity is a holistic framework in which the whole data lifecycle is handled within one unified platform.

questions.stem: Which paradigm is Data Platform Gravity said to be inspired by?
questions.explanation: Data Platform Gravity is inspired by the Data Fabric paradigm, advocating seamless operations across the entire data lifecycle.

questions.stem: Which inefficiency is named as a consequence of the fragmented, multi-tool approach that Data Platform Gravity seeks to replace?
options: Data duplication, integration challenges and increased costs
questions.explanation: The fragmented approach introduces inefficiencies such as data duplication, integration challenges and increased costs.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a core component of a Data Platform Gravity system?
questions.explanation: The core components are Data Ingestion, Data Transformation, Data Science and Machine Learning, Business Intelligence, and Data Integration and Sharing.

questions.stem: How does building BI dashboards directly within a Data Platform Gravity system benefit reporting?
options: It removes the need for any data transformation
It allows dashboards to be sold to competitors
It eliminates the need for data ingestion
It eliminates the need to export data to third-party tools, preserving data integrity and enabling near-real-time reporting
questions.explanation: Building BI within the platform avoids exporting data to third-party tools, which preserves data integrity and enables near-real-time reporting.

questions.stem: Which benefit of Data Platform Gravity refers to reducing the latency between data ingestion and actionable insights?
questions.explanation: Faster time-to-insight comes from integrated workflows that reduce the latency between ingestion and actionable insights.

questions.stem: How does Data Platform Gravity deliver cost efficiency?
options: Fewer tools mean reduced licensing costs, lower infrastructure requirements and simplified support overheads
By storing data only in cache
By charging consumers for each query
questions.explanation: Consolidating onto fewer tools reduces licensing costs, lowers infrastructure requirements and simplifies support overheads.

questions.stem: What is recommended to mitigate the vendor lock-in risk of Data Platform Gravity?
options: Buying the most expensive platform available
Choosing a platform that adheres to open standards
Keeping all legacy tools running in parallel indefinitely
Disabling data sharing with external systems
questions.explanation: Because relying on a single platform can limit future flexibility, choosing a platform that adheres to open standards is essential.

questions.stem: Which of the following is listed as a challenge of adopting Data Platform Gravity?
options: Reduced learning curve for new users
questions.explanation: Migrating from a fragmented ecosystem to a unified platform requires careful planning to integrate or decommission legacy systems.

questions.stem: Which future capability of Data Platform Gravity refers to automated cleaning, enriching and governing of data using AI-driven insights?
questions.explanation: Autonomous data management is the anticipated future capability of automating data cleaning, enrichment and governance with AI-driven insights.
